triage.module_scope_rationale: F2P lives in flink-tests/flink-runtime/flink-datastream for generalized-watermark behavior. P2P uses independent original flink-clients selectors so unrelated client-facing behavior is pinned before and after the patch.

fixture_taint_summary: eval_tests.patch contains only the selected WatermarkITCase system scenarios. Non-selected unit/helper/baseline test hunks from the PR are kept in omitted.patch so pre-state P2P is not tainted by test code that imports generalized-watermark implementation symbols.

mutant_set_revision.note: mutant_014 was previously removed as §6-unreachable because forcing the source-side WatermarkEvent alignment flag to false in SourceOperator is observable only via PR-added/internal symbols. The post-audit cleanup also removed the process-side aligned selector for the same reason: the active F2P set now tests the FLIP-visible combineWaitForAllChannels behavior without requiring the PR-specific Alignable* declarations or WatermarkEvent alignment flag. The unselected SourceOperatorGeneralizedWatermarkAugTest and WatermarkOperatorAugTest hunks were also removed from the augmented patch compile surface because they imported internal PR-added runtime classes without being selected F2P/P2P.

coverage_gate.measurement_note: JaCoCo line coverage over executable Java lines added by solution.patch; union mode runs original plus augmented F2P/P2P selectors.
coverage_gate.post_audit_note: Coverage figures are historical from the pre-cleanup augmented patch and were not rerun after removing unselected internal-import hunks from eval_tests_aug.patch.

triage.test_level_policy: Augmented FLIP-467 F2P selectors exercise generalized watermark declaration/value behavior through FLIP-visible Watermark APIs in flink-tests. Augmented P2P selectors run in the unrelated flink-clients retry package and do not import generalized watermark symbols.

org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WatermarkDeclarations.newBuilder(...).typeLong/typeBool().build(), LongWatermarkDeclaration, BoolWatermarkDeclaration, LongWatermark, BoolWatermark, and WatermarkCombinationPolicy getters.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: Builds long and bool declarations without optional builder calls and verifies the FLIP-specified default MIN and AND combination policies, default FORWARD handling, and produced watermark identifiers/values. This makes flipped builder defaults observable through the public declaration surface.

requirement_sections: Proposed Changes > Handle Watermarks in Process Function
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: WatermarkDeclarations long/bool builders using combineFunctionMax, combineFunctionMin, combineFunctionOR, combineFunctionAND, combineWaitForAllChannels, defaultHandlingStrategyIgnore, and defaultHandlingStrategyForward.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: Uses explicit public builder calls and verifies the selected combination function, wait-for-all flag, and default handling strategy. Distinct chained calls catch ignored setters and wrong enum assignments directly from the public declaration object.
Pins the public policy object invariant that combineWaitForAllChannels is preserved by the policy object used by watermark combination.

org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.public_surface: LongWatermark, BoolWatermark, LongWatermarkDeclaration, and BoolWatermarkDeclaration constructors and getters through public watermark declaration/value APIs.
org.apache.flink.test.streaming.api.data.rationale: Covers the FLIP-visible watermark value and declaration accessors without requiring PR-specific equality, hashing, or string formatting behavior.

org.apache.flink.client.program.rest.ret.rationale: Pins an unrelated public client retry cap behavior so generalized watermark changes do not regress adjacent client functionality outside the modified watermark modules.
Pins the existing negative-attempt validation in flink-clients, a P2P stability surface independent of generalized watermark declarations and runtime emission.
